library_preparation_preflight.summary: A prior automated attempt on this exact issue (preserved on branch ai/vjovanov/human-intervention/issue-8723-...) reached BUILD SUCCESSFUL for both JVM and native tests using only standard testImplementation deps (spring-boot-quartz, spring-boot-autoconfigure, spring-boot-test, assertj-core) and the default in-memory RAMJobStore scheduler. No Docker image, non-standard dependency, or env/system property was required; the job was only flagged for human intervention due to an unrelated Forge finalization/metrics-publication bug after the library tests already passed.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Quartz autoconfiguration defaults to RAMJobStore (in-memory) — no datasource/Docker container is needed for core coverage. Expect native-image metadata gaps on first fixTestNativeImageRun pass for: reflection on org.springframework.boot.quartz.autoconfigure.QuartzAutoConfiguration (constructor + quartzScheduler factory method) and QuartzProperties (all declared ctors/methods/fields); a conditional reflection entry for org.springframework.transaction.PlatformTransactionManager gated on QuartzAutoConfiguration being reached; and a conditional reflection entry for org.springframework.scheduling.quartz.ResourceLoaderClassLoadHelper gated on SchedulerFactoryBean being reached. These are normal reachability-metadata.json additions, not extra setup — add them if checkMetadataFiles/native test surfaces them. If a test injects a Spring bean into a Quartz Job instance, make sure the setter is annotated @Autowired (a prior run's test initially failed an assertion because this annotation was missing on AutowiringQuartzJob#setMessageService).
